title: Deep vein thrombosis (India)
specialty: Internal Medicine / Vascular Surgery / Haematology / Emergency Medicine

evidenceAudit.scope: Suspected and confirmed lower-limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in adults in India: Wells score, compression ultrasound, D-dimer, anticoagulant choice including renal impairment, cancer and pregnancy, and duration, using NICE NG158, the ESC 2019 pulmonary embolism guideline (for anticoagulant regimens) and US labels, because no Indian national VTE guideline was found.
findings: Two-level DVT Wells score (2 or more likely), proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 hours, D-dimer, interim anticoagulation, apixaban or rivaroxaban first line, alternatives, renal-impairment choices, cancer, duration and thrombophilia advice checked against NICE NG158.
DOAC, dabigatran, edoxaban and warfarin regimens checked against the ESC 2019 summary; apixaban, dabigatran and enoxaparin doses against US labels.
unverifiedSections: No Indian national VTE guideline was found; NICE NG158 and ESC 2019 are used.
Rivaroxaban and edoxaban doses are from the ACC summary of ESC 2019, not their labels.
Paediatric VTE dosing is given only for apixaban (label); other paediatric doses are outside the cited sources.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Deep vein thrombosis is clot in the deep veins, usually of the leg, arising from Virchow's triad: venous stasis, endothelial injury and hypercoagulability. In India, common triggers include surgery, long immobilisation, trauma, pregnancy and the postpartum period, cancer, tuberculosis and dehydration. Proximal DVT can embolise to the lungs. Diagnosis combines the two-level Wells score with D-dimer and compression ultrasound (NICE NG158). Treatment is anticoagulation for at least 3 months, preferably with a direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) such as apixaban or rivaroxaban; low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) is used in pregnancy, severe renal failure and some cancers.
keyMechanisms: Stasis, endothelial injury and hypercoagulability (Virchow's triad) start thrombus in valve pockets.
Clot propagates proximally and obstructs venous return, causing swelling and pain.
Proximal clot can detach and cause pulmonary embolism.
Valve damage leads to post-thrombotic syndrome.

symptoms: Unilateral calf or thigh pain and swelling
Breathlessness or chest pain if PE
physicalSigns: Calf swelling 3 cm or more than the other side
Pitting oedema of the symptomatic leg
redFlags: Breathlessness, chest pain, haemoptysis: suspect pulmonary embolism
Active bleeding or very high bleeding risk

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Erythema, warmth, fever, skin entry point.
Popliteal swelling, knee arthritis; ultrasound shows cyst.

differentials.condition: Bilateral oedema from heart, liver or kidney disease

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Two-level DVT Wells score 2 or more.
Wells score 1 or less: D-dimer first.
At least 3 months; provoked: consider stopping at 3 months; unprovoked: consider continuing.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess probability
actions: Likely: ultrasound within 4 hours; if not possible, D-dimer, interim anticoagulation and ultrasound within 24 hours (NICE NG158).
Unlikely: D-dimer; ultrasound only if positive (NICE NG158).

clinicalManagement.title: Anticoagulate
actions: Apixaban or rivaroxaban first line (NICE NG158).
Alternatives: LMWH for at least 5 days then dabigatran or edoxaban; or LMWH with warfarin until INR 2.0 or more on two readings (NICE NG158).
CrCl below 15 mL/min: LMWH or UFH, or with VKA (NICE NG158).

clinicalManagement.title: Duration
actions: At least 3 months for all (NICE NG158).
Provoked with factor resolved: consider stopping at 3 months (NICE NG158).
Unprovoked: consider continuing; weigh HAS-BLED (NICE NG158).

clinicalManagement.title: Review
actions: Review at least yearly if anticoagulation continues (NICE NG158).
Do not offer cancer screening unless symptoms or signs (NICE NG158).

branches.label: DOAC pathway
branches.entryCriteria: Confirmed proximal DVT, CrCl 15 mL/min or more, not pregnant, no antiphospholipid syndrome.

branches.label: LMWH pathway
branches.entryCriteria: Pregnancy, CrCl below 15 mL/min, triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome, or DOAC unsuitable.

regimens.dose: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily
regimens.duration: At least 3 months; after 6 months 2.5 mg twice daily may reduce recurrence
adjustments: Paediatric: Children from birth: weight-based (for example 35 kg or more 10 mg twice daily for 7 days then 5 mg twice daily) after at least 5 days of initial anticoagulation (label section 2.2).
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: No adjustment in adults including dialysis (label); children: not if eGFR below 30.
CLD: Child-Pugh B: no recommendation; C: not recommended.

regimens.dose: 15 mg twice daily for 3 weeks, then 20 mg once daily
adjustments: Paediatric: Not covered by the cited sources.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Avoid if CrCl below 15 mL/min (NICE: options for 15–50 mL/min).
CLD: Avoid in moderate or severe liver disease.

regimens.useWhen: Apixaban and rivaroxaban unsuitable; after LMWH for 5 days (NICE NG158).

regimens.dose: 1 mg/kg every 12 hours, or 1.5 mg/kg once daily (inpatient)
regimens.duration: At least 5 days and until INR 2–3 if switching to warfarin; whole course in pregnancy or cancer
adjustments: Paediatric: Paediatric safety not established (label).
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: CrCl below 30 mL/min: 1 mg/kg once daily (label); below 15 mL/min prefer UFH.
CLD: No adjustment stated.
regimens.sourceTitle: Enoxaparin sodium injection (Lovenox), US prescribing information (DailyMed)

regimens.indication: Long-term treatment after LMWH (not in pregnancy)
regimens.dose: 5 mg daily (10 mg in healthy adults under 60) adjusted to INR 2–3
adjustments: Paediatric: Not covered by the cited sources.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: No dose change; monitor INR more often.
CLD: Liver disease raises effect; monitor INR.
Overlap with LMWH for at least 5 days and until INR 2.0 or more on two consecutive readings (NICE NG158).

medicationPlan.note: Drug choice follows NICE NG158; regimens from US labels and the ESC 2019 summary. No Indian national VTE guideline was found. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

learningObjectives: Use the Wells score with D-dimer and ultrasound.
Choose an anticoagulant by renal function and pregnancy.
keyPoints: Wells 2 or more: ultrasound within 4 hours.
Apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily.
pitfalls: DOAC in pregnancy or antiphospholipid syndrome.
Wrong enoxaparin dose in kidney disease.

patientEducation: Take the anticoagulant at the same time daily; never double a missed dose.
Seek help for breathlessness, chest pain or bleeding.
Tell every doctor and dentist you are on an anticoagulant.
mdtReferrals: Haematology for antiphospholipid syndrome or recurrent VTE
dischargeCriteria: Written information and contact details given (NICE NG158)
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review at 3 months to decide duration; yearly if continuing (NICE NG158).
